## Summary

Research confidence is **Low**. Sources do not yet confirm this break's best wind. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best wind direction.
- Sources disagree about the wave size this break works in.
- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- No survey or peer-reviewed study of the bottom was found.

| Variable | Research confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Swell direction | High | Supported by 9 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Swell size | Low | Supported by 4 independent sources, including a surf magazine; 1 disagrees. |
| Swell period | Moderate | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Wind | Low | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a community source; 4 disagree. |
| Tide | Low | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a community source; 2 disagree. |
| Bottom / bathymetry | Moderate | Described by 7 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry. |
| Season | High | Supported by 10 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry. |
| How the wave breaks | High | Described by 7 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Wind is now a two-sided conflict. East/east-northeast as offshore or best: Surf-Forecast ENE, WannaSurf E/NE, LatAm Surfing E, MyWaveFinder E; all 60-82 deg from the profile's 150. Southeast as best: Chicama Surf Trips (local operator, 2024) and Surf Escape (2023); both 15 deg from 150. Wikipedia and a WannaSurf user comment say only that the wind is (predominantly) offshore. Surfing-Waves says the prevailing winds are south/southwest. So no direct source supports SSE (150) exactly. The weight of descriptive sources leans E. A value of about 90-135 would fit more of them than 150. Swell size: Wikipedia (the only source that converts its scale) says the main point holds at least 10 ft Hawaiian, about 20 ft faces, above the profile max of 12. Several guides put the best range at 4-7 ft (scale not stated). Period: the only numeric source is Topologica (14-18 s). It is undated, of unknown authorship and possibly machine-generated, so treat it as low weight. Other sources say only long-period groundswell. Tide: WannaSurf, MyWaveFinder and Surf Escape say all tides, matching the profile. Topologica says mid-incoming to high to connect the sections, and Surfer Today (unread) said low to mid. Season: March/April-October/November across eight publishers, consistent with the profile's March-October. NASA Earth Observatory is classed official (a US government Earth-science agency; its text quotes a University of Maine oceanographer). No peer-reviewed study or measured bathymetry of the Chicama wave was found (Crossref returned only fisheries, archaeology and 1960s water-temperature papers for Puerto Chicama). A Spanish-language search for thesis or modelling work found nothing specific.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 3 ft [S3] · about 4 ft on the point (8 ft on the swell charts); smaller waves weak and slow [S1] | conflicting | S1, S3 | `wave_height_min_ft` 3 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | 4–6 ft | documented | S4, S8, S13 | no separate setting; working range 3–12 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 12–20 ft | documented | S1, S3 | `wave_height_max_ft` 12 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at less than 1 m / 3 ft (scale not stated), while Wikipedia says waves under about 4 ft on the point, which it equates with 8 ft on the swell charts (offshore), tend to be quite weak and slow.
  - S3 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at Less than 1m / 3ft and holds up to 4m+ / 12ft”
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “waves less than about 4 feet on the point (i.e. 8 feet on the swell charts) tend to be quite weak and slow”
- **Ideal range**: Surfer Today (search summary) gives a best size of chest to head high (4-6 ft) and LatAm Surfing solid rides at 4-6 ft (scale not stated); Topologica says 5-7 ft faces for all four points to connect.
  - S4 (Surfer Today): “Its listed best swell direction is S-SW, with a best size of chest to head-high (4-6 feet)”
  - S8 (LatAm Surfing): “you can get solid rides when its in the 4-6 foot range”
  - S13 (Topologica): “When swell direction (pure southwest 200-220°), period (14-18 seconds), tide (mid-incoming to high), and size (5-7ft faces) align perfectly, all four points connect”
- **Maximum suitable**: WannaSurf's top bracket is 4 m+ / 12 ft (open-ended) and Wikipedia says the main point holds at least 10 ft Hawaiian scale, which it converts itself to about 20 ft faces; both are lower bounds, so they do not contradict each other.
  - S3 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at Less than 1m / 3ft and holds up to 4m+ / 12ft”
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “the main point will hold at least 10 feet Hawaiian scale (i.e. about 20 feet faces)”

  - S7 (Actualidad Ambiental (SPDA)): “Proyectos portuarios, alteraciones en la dinámica de la arena y la presión de la industria extractiva han sido amenazas recurrentes.”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at less than 1 m / 3 ft (scale not stated), while Wikipedia says waves under about 4 ft on the point, which it equates with 8 ft on the swell charts (offshore), tend to be quite weak and slow.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast says offshore winds blow from the east-northeast and WannaSurf, LatAm Surfing and MyWaveFinder give east (or east and northeast) as the good or ideal wind, while Chicama Surf Trips says best wind is offshore from the southeast and Surf Escape gives a southeast wind as best; E-NE and SE are 67-90 deg apart.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: WannaSurf, MyWaveFinder and Surf Escape say all (any) tides, Surfer Today (search summary) says low to mid, and Topologica says mid-incoming to high is needed for all four points to connect.
